Era Explorer

Every tour player since 1991 on one point-level rating scale (15 million points), and every Open Era player on a results-only scale behind it. Compare careers, weigh eras, rank the hardest title runs, and build your own GOAT list.

Ratings over time

A player's rating says how they'd fare against the average tour player of the whole period — 0 is that average. Serve and return are rated separately. Hard, clay and grass count equally. Surface ratings use career results, and small samples stay closer to a player's overall level.

Title runs, ranked by the draw

Every tour-level title since 1968 scored two ways. Path difficulty asks how often a standard top-5 player would win that exact draw — each opponent at their rating that quarter, on that surface — so it belongs to the draw, not the champion. Execution asks how far above the model's expectation the champion actually played.

1991 onward uses the point-level model. Before 1991 only results exist, so those runs (marked results only) come from a match-level rating that is anchored to each era's rank 11–50 player; compare them among themselves rather than against the point-level runs.

Build your own GOAT list

Six measured components on one scale, no title counting. Move the weights; the list, the scores and the rank intervals recompute live. The default weights are one defensible opinion, not a verdict.

Peak and sustained excellence are Elo-like ratings from the point model (1991→) or, before that, the results-only model mapped onto the same axis with its extra uncertainty (results only and mixed careers). Hardware is every tour title, weighted by how rarely a standard top-5 player wins that exact draw, in "standard slams" — a typical Masters is worth about half a slam, a typical 250 about a seventh.
